newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares power to close after U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares power to close after U.S. CPI.

text.p: South African shares powered ahead to finish Tuesday on a high following a better-than-expected U.S. CPI number and were further propelled by an early jump on Wall Street.
Dealers said that shares had been treading water awaiting the release of the U.S. data which would remove uncertainty from Wall Street and other markets.
U.S. March Consumer Price inflation rose 0.1 percent compared to a 0.3 percent rise in February. Analysts had expected a 0.2 percent rise.

After Wall Street's 148-point plunge last Friday, local stocks have been anxiously waiting for the U.S. market to settle down. Many believed there would be a further correction on Wall Street and that Monday's firmer close could not be taken to seriously.
But dealers were saying late on Tuesday that things were starting to look much better for equities worldwide.
Volumes for the day were fair to large, improving particularly when market uncertainty evaporated.
Gold shares continued to disappoint, dipping from the start of trade and shedding more in later as investors climbed into industrials, dragging the gold index to its lowest level in 17 months.
Industrials added 70.7 points to 8,237.5 points, all-shares climbed 30.9 points to 6,997.3 and golds lost 12.6 to 1,270.7.
